title: Union Find
subtitle: Maintain a partition that only merges: representatives answer connectivity while root metadata summarizes each component.
variables: N = number of initialized elements, E = input edges, Q = queries, M = total DSU operations, α = inverse Ackermann function, A = number of accounts, H = email occurrences, U = unique emails, R*C = grid positions; L = output/query text length; U_g = distinct emails in output group g; E_lifetimes = number of active edge intervals in offline mixed-update problems. With union by size/rank plus path compression, M operations cost O(N+M α(N)) amortized total after initialization; a single operation is not guaranteed O(1). Weighted/rollback variants have explicitly different bounds. Dictionary-backed labels use expected hashing; hashing and comparing a long string costs O(length) initially/worst-case, and sorting strings adds comparison cost. Main bounds use fixed-width numeric arithmetic; Python large integers have additional bit complexity. Space separates initialized DSU arrays, constructed/sorted input copies, auxiliary stacks and returned output. Templates use standard-library Python 3.10+, integer IDs 0..N-1 unless explicitly mapped; root identifiers are unstable implementation details. I = positive-multiplicity edge lifetime intervals in the mixed-update template (I≤Q); rational-potential arithmetic has numerator/denominator bit costs beyond pointer-operation bounds. Hash expectations are not adversarial guarantees: many colliding keys can make a lookup linear in table size. For empty strings an O(L) walk means O(1+L) including fixed call/root work. Python list append/pop may resize linearly on a single call; amortized bounds apply over sequences. Under size/rank balancing, a single compressed find still has O(log N) worst-case pointer work; the stronger inverse-Ackermann claim is amortized across operations.

fundamentalDetails.why: Connectivity is an equivalence relation; an efficient partition need not preserve graph routes.
fundamentalDetails.result: parent roots 0 and 2 describe groups {0,1} and {2,3}.
fundamentalDetails.edge: A parent link can be invented by balancing and is not an original edge.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: DSU stores which group, not how to travel.

fundamentalDetails.why: Representative equality is transitive while immediate-parent equality is not.
fundamentalDetails.result: Element 2 follows 2→1→0 even though parent[2] differs from parent[0].
fundamentalDetails.edge: A singleton root points to itself; never use -1 as a parent sentinel accidentally.

fundamentalDetails.why: Smaller-to-larger attachment limits how often any element can gain depth.
fundamentalDetails.use: Bound height before path compression is considered.
fundamentalDetails.edge: Only root sizes remain authoritative; losing size entries may stay stale.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: Depth rises only when component size at least doubles.

fundamentalDetails.why: Repeated finds can shorten future paths without changing membership.
fundamentalDetails.result: The find ends at root 0 and shortens parent[3] from 2 to 1.
fundamentalDetails.edge: The illustrated halving is not full flattening of every traversed node.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: Compression changes structure, not the partition.

fundamentalDetails.why: Nearly constant total work is a sequence guarantee, not a per-call magic constant.
fundamentalDetails.result: Three doublings grow a component from 1 to 8.
fundamentalDetails.edge: An unbalanced, uncompressed chain can still make a find linear.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: Balancing gives log depth; compression gives stronger amortized work.

fundamentalDetails.why: A repeated relation must not count as another group merge.
fundamentalDetails.use: Maintain components or root aggregates correctly.
fundamentalDetails.edge: A self-loop is always a no-op union but may indicate a cycle-forming graph edge.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: Update count and aggregates only after different roots merge.

fundamentalDetails.why: Domain meaning belongs in explicit metadata, not an arbitrary representative ID.
fundamentalDetails.use: Track component sums, sizes, minima or boolean flags.
fundamentalDetails.result: Root 0 now holds sum 12 after linking root 1.
fundamentalDetails.edge: Non-associative aggregates or instantaneous member-list queries need more design.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: Root aggregate summarizes exactly its current class.

fundamentalDetails.why: Every successful undirected union adds one forest edge and removes one component.
fundamentalDetails.use: Detect redundant edges or validate a tree.
fundamentalDetails.result: 5 vertices and 2 components require 3 successful forest edges.
fundamentalDetails.edge: Directed acyclic triangle edges may be redundant after directions are discarded.

fundamentalDetails.why: Monotone eligibility permits sharing one DSU across many otherwise repeated searches.
fundamentalDetails.result: Original query indices are processed in order [1,0].
fundamentalDetails.edge: Equal threshold weight is excluded for strict queries; sorting must not reorder final answers.

fundamentalDetails.why: Temporary merges can be undone cheaply only if every structural change is reversible.
fundamentalDetails.result: History returns to snapshot 0 after popping its one logged record.
fundamentalDetails.edge: Snapshot numbers are ancestor prefixes, not immutable versions valid after arbitrary branching.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: No compression; log and undo successful root attachments.

fundamentalDetails.why: Relative constraints need orientation-aware composition, not just connectivity.
fundamentalDetails.use: Maintain same/different parity or multiplicative potentials.
fundamentalDetails.result: Two xor-one links compose to parity zero from node 2 to root 0.
fundamentalDetails.edge: Xor reverses symmetrically; ratio weights reverse by reciprocal, not xor.
fundamentalDetails.takeaway: Write the potential equation before the union formula.

steps: Initialize every element as its own root and component.
For each added undirected link find both roots, attach smaller component to larger.
Answer connectivity by root equality; compress on finds for amortized performance.
templates: Balanced DSU with iterative path halving
patternDetails.related: Undirected cycle / redundant edge; Components and root aggregates
patternDetails.variations: For static graphs DFS/BFS may be simpler and provide paths. Unknown sparse labels need a map and deliberate universe growth.

steps: Keep sizes or associative aggregates only at current roots.
After successful union merge metadata and decrement component count once.
For a proposed island flip, deduplicate neighboring roots before summing sizes.
templates: Balanced DSU with iterative path halving
Largest island after at most one flip
patternDetails.variations: For minimum member keep explicit min metadata rather than forcing minimum root ID. DSU does not enumerate members without a separate scan or maintained lists.

steps: Process each undirected edge in the required input order.
Different roots mean accept edge and merge.
Equal roots mean a cycle-forming/redundant edge; record first, last or every such edge per contract.
patternDetails.variations: A valid tree also needs connectivity or N−1 successful links under a nonempty-universe convention. DSU alone does not solve directed redundant-connection rules.

steps: Copy/sort undirected edges by weight.
Take an edge iff it joins different current components.
Accumulate cost/chosen edges, then reject disconnected input if an MST was required.
templates: Kruskal minimum spanning tree with chosen edges
patternDetails.related: Undirected cycle / redundant edge; Offline threshold queries
patternDetails.variations: Negative edges and weight ties are valid. Dense implicit point graphs may prefer O(N²)-time/O(N)-space Prim over materializing O(N²) edges.

steps: Map each exact identifier to its first observed owner.
Union accounts sharing identifiers, not merely display names.
Group unique identifiers by final root and apply the specified name/order policy.
templates: Merge accounts by shared email identity
patternDetails.related: Components and root aggregates; Incremental connectivity
patternDetails.variations: Fuzzy matching is not automatic equivalence. Same-row/column stone connections use distinct label namespaces and a separate modeling proof.

steps: Mark water slots inactive even though dense DSU arrays exist for all cells.
On first activation add one island.
Union active bounded neighbors and subtract one island for each successful merge; duplicates do nothing.
patternDetails.related: Components and root aggregates; Reverse-time deletions
patternDetails.variations: For huge sparse grids map only activated coordinates. The dense dsu.components includes inactive slots, so it is not the active island count.

steps: Sort weighted edges and indexed queries by threshold.
Before a query union every newly eligible edge with weight strictly less than its limit.
Compare roots and store answer at original query index.
patternDetails.variations: Use ≤ only if the question allows equality. The same-vertex zero-edge path is valid regardless of a low threshold.

steps: Count pending deletion requests per original edge ID.
Build the final graph from edges never deleted.
Walk deletions backward, record current count first, and reinsert an edge only when its remaining deletion count becomes zero.
templates: Reverse-time edge deletions with duplicate requests
patternDetails.related: Activation on grids; Rollback DSU / time segments
patternDetails.variations: Vertex removals similarly reverse to activation. Bricks Falling additionally needs stable-to-roof size differences and duplicate-hit handling, not raw component counts.

steps: Convert each positive edge-multiplicity lifetime to a half-open time interval.
Place intervals in a time segment tree and save a DSU snapshot on node entry.
Apply node edges, answer leaf queries, and rollback to entry snapshot on exit.
templates: Offline mixed edge updates with time-segment rollback
patternDetails.variations: No path compression; union by size gives log depth. Duplicate edges require multiplicity lifetime tracking; rollback tokens refer only to current ancestors.

steps: Write the relative-potential equation to parent before writing code.
Find composes xor or multiplication along root paths.
For different roots derive the link potential in the chosen orientation; for same roots verify the equation.
templates: Parity constraints with balanced relative-xor DSU
patternDetails.related: Incremental connectivity; Rollback DSU / time segments
patternDetails.variations: Parity uses xor and symmetric inversion. Ratios use multiplication/reciprocal; exact Fractions avoid float tolerance at extra bit cost. Inequalities need a different model.

templateDetails.preconditions: Fixed universe integer IDs 0..n-1, n≥0. find returns unstable representative; union mutates partition and returns whether merged; component_size reads root size. Invalid size/ID raises ValueError. find also mutates parent pointers; no path output or deletions. Empty DSU has zero components but no valid find.
templateDetails.observation: Root IDs can change; find also mutates structure without changing connectivity.

templateDetails.preconditions: Undirected edge iterable; fixed integer IDs checked by DSU. Returns final component count and input indices of every cycle-forming edge in input order, not necessarily the one special edge a particular LC task asks for. Self-loops/parallel edges included. No caller input mutation; n=0 empty edges returns (0,[]).
templateDetails.observation: Successful edges form a forest; failed edges are redundant in this processed order.

templateDetails.preconditions: Undirected (u,v,finite numeric weight) iterable; negative weights and duplicates allowed. Returns (minimum total, chosen original graph edges), None if disconnected. Empty graph returns (0,[]); singleton returns zero even with self-loops. Caller edges not sorted or mutated; ties may select any MST.
templateDetails.observation: Sorting chooses a safe cut edge; DSU only checks whether it closes a cycle.

templateDetails.preconditions: Sequence accounts=[name,email,...], strings case-sensitive and identifier equality exact. Shared email joins accounts, names alone never do. Assumes names within a connected identity are compatible; output uses earliest original account name, groups ordered by earliest index, distinct emails sorted. No-email accounts retained separately, [] input→[], empty account record raises ValueError. No caller input mutation or email-list slicing.
templateDetails.observation: Identifier equality provides evidence; shared display names alone do not. Root-map insertion order already follows first account index, avoiding an unnecessary O(A log A) group sort.

templateDetails.preconditions: Undirected edges=(u,v,numeric weight), queries=(u,v,numeric strict limit), reusable or one-pass iterables copied internally. Returns booleans in original query order. A zero-edge path from a vertex to itself is always valid. Equal-weight edges are excluded at limit. n≥0/endpoints validated; finite comparable numeric values assumed; no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Strict thresholds exclude equal-weight edges and outputs retain query order.

templateDetails.preconditions: Initially all-water rectangular grid, four-neighbor land adjacency; additions iterable of coordinate pairs. Duplicate additions no-op. Returns count after each addition; zero-sized grid plus no additions→[], invalid coordinate raises ValueError. Dense DSU initializes water slots too, so its components field is NOT island count; separate count tracks active roots. Caller input unchanged.
templateDetails.observation: Dense DSU includes water; maintain a separate active-island count.

templateDetails.preconditions: Rectangular 0/1 grid, four-direction islands; returns maximum land component size after changing at most one zero to one. Empty shapes→0, all-water nonempty→1, all-land→RC. Deduplicates neighboring roots so the same island is not counted twice. Input unchanged; invalid shape/value raises ValueError.
templateDetails.observation: A flipped cell may touch the same root multiple times, so deduplicate.

templateDetails.preconditions: Fixed nonnegative n, integer IDs. snapshot returns current history length, rollback restores that ancestor prefix and discards later merges. Tokens valid only for the current ancestral history, NOT persistent versions across diverging branches. No-op union logs nothing; rollback counts successful merges, not method calls. No compression; caller must manage segment-tree/time-interval scheduling separately.
templateDetails.observation: Undo only successful attachments in reverse; compression is intentionally absent.

templateDetails.preconditions: Constraint color[a] xor color[b] == required (0=same,1=different). constrain returns True for accepted/redundant-consistent constraint, False for contradiction and leaves state unchanged on contradiction; caller decides whether to retain a global inconsistency flag. relation returns known parity or None if unrelated. Fixed IDs validated, no compression to keep relative metadata simple; xor root link is orientation-symmetric, unlike generic additive/ratio potentials.
templateDetails.observation: Xor root-link inversion is symmetric, unlike ratio orientation.

templateDetails.preconditions: Fixed universe and undirected indexed edges initially present; deletions are input edge IDs and repeated deletion of an already absent edge is a no-op. Returns component count after each forward deletion, including isolated vertices. Parallel edges have independent IDs. Inputs copied, not mutated. Reverse reinsertion waits until all duplicate requests have been undone. This is ordinary deletion connectivity, not roof-stability/bricks accounting.
templateDetails.observation: Delay reinsertion until every duplicate deletion request is undone.

templateDetails.preconditions: Initially empty undirected multigraph, operations (add/remove/query,u,v). Add increases edge multiplicity; remove decreases one and rejects absent edge; connectivity cares only whether multiplicity>0. Returns query booleans in chronological order. I=positive-multiplicity lifetime intervals, at most Q. No input mutation; dictionaries expected. Parent traversal iterative; the two scheduling helpers recurse only O(log Q), not graph depth. Apply intervals [add,remove), rollback to entry snapshot on every segment exit.
templateDetails.observation: Every segment exit restores its entry partition before the sibling runs.

templateDetails.preconditions: Known integer-ID universe; constrain(a,b,v) enforces potential[a]/potential[b]=positive rational v. Prefer int, Fraction or rational/decimal strings for exact semantics; Fraction(float) means the exact binary float, not its displayed decimal. Returns False without mutation on contradictory same-root equation, True on accepted/redundant relation; caller tracks global inconsistency if needed. relation returns Fraction or None. weight[x]=potential[x]/potential[parent[x]], no compression. Balancing bounds pointer depth, NOT rational numerator/denominator bit cost. For conventional floating LC399, use tolerance and finite nonzero intermediate arithmetic; do not substitute xor root-link equations.
templateDetails.observation: Link ratio follows algebra and reverses by reciprocal when balancing flips orientation.

practiceDetails.insight: Foundation — A DSU partition captures all processed undirected links; a one-shot traversal may be simpler. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Undirected; static BFS also works.

Foundation — Initialize isolates, then union true matrix entries; the matrix scan dominates input processing. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Do not double-count components on symmetric edges.

Foundation — A failed union identifies a cycle-forming edge in processed order; adapt last/first return policy. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Problem’s 1-based labels require mapping; last redundant policy.

Foundation — Connected and acyclic is the definition; N−1 edges alone is not enough without the other condition. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: N-1 edge condition plus connectivity; self-loops and parallel edges.

Transfer — At least N−1 total cables are necessary; if enough, connecting C components takes C−1 rewires. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Need at least N-1 cables; answer components-1.

Transfer — Collapse all equality classes first; only afterward check inequalities against final roots. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Process all equalities before testing inequalities.

Transfer — Shared identifiers establish transitive identity; equal names alone do not. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Names alone do not identify accounts.

Transfer — Each stone links one row namespace to one column namespace; answer stones minus nonempty connected groups. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Row 0 and column 0 need separate namespaces.

Transfer — Deduplicate values and merge consecutive neighbors; a start-only set scan improves to expected O(N). Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Deduplicate values; DSU is optional overhead.

Transfer — A balanced root is arbitrary, so carry the minimum character as separate root metadata. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Balanced root ID need not be minimum character.

Transfer — Kruskal needs quadratic complete edges; dense implicit Prim often saves memory. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Materializing complete graph edges costs quadratic memory.

Transfer — Activation creates an island only once; each successful active-neighbor union removes one. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Duplicate activations and non-square bounds.

Transfer — The candidate size is one plus sizes of distinct adjacent roots, not one per adjacent direction. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Same neighboring island may touch flipped cell from multiple directions.

Transfer — Eligible edges form nested subgraphs when queries are sorted by strict limit. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Strict < limit; restore query order.

Stretch — Shared edges can benefit both travelers, so use them before exclusive edges in separate DSUs. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Use type-3 edges before exclusive ones; both travelers must connect.

Stretch — Reverse hits into activations, compare roof-connected sizes, and subtract the restored brick itself. This is a roof-stability adaptation, not the raw deletion-count template. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Exclude restored brick itself; duplicate hits need careful accounting.
practiceDetails.secondary: Reverse time; sentinel roof; duplicate hits

practiceDetails.insight: Stretch — A connected component of allowed index swaps permits every permutation of its characters. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Any permutation within a connected index component is reachable.

Stretch — Relative ratios compose along a parent chain; link orientation must preserve a/b=value. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Map variable names to IDs; unknown variables return -1 externally. Exact rational template is not tolerant floating-point consistency checking.

decisionProcess: 0–25 seconds — Confirm the relationship is undirected connectivity/equivalence and updates only merge. If shortest path, directed reachability, or an actual route is needed, choose traversal instead.

25–50 seconds — Define the universe including isolates and label mapping; decide duplicate/self-loop policy. Basic fixed-ID DSU uses size balancing plus iterative path compression; state O(N+M α(N)) amortized, not worst-case constant.

50–80 seconds — Identify the extra question: failed union detects an undirected cycle edge; root sizes/sums require metadata; MST uses sorted Kruskal; identity merging uses exact identifier owners; land additions require separate active flags.

80–110 seconds — If queries can be reordered and eligibility grows, sort thresholds and preserve original indices. Deletions-only known in advance may reverse to insertions; mixed updates need lifetimes plus rollback without compression.

110–145 seconds — For constraints write the equation: parity uses xor, ratios multiply and invert. Same-root inconsistent constraints reject; do not force semantic minimum IDs to be structural roots. Explain why naive deletion or unlogged compression fails.

145–180 seconds — Quote initialization, sorting copies, hashing, output and potential bit costs. Test repeated union, isolate, root change, strict equality threshold and duplicate activation; then an odd parity cycle, ratio orientation or rollback branch as applicable.
